newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended weak on Thursday as poor sentiment from the gold price knocked prices in quiet trade.
"The market is definitely easier with gold trading below 350. The negative sentiment from golds seems to have filtered into industrials," dealers said.
They said some profit-taking also hit industrial shares after institutions had been putting new money in the system since beginning of the month.
The better-than-expected trade data cheered the market briefly in the afternoon after drifting lower amid a lack of direction and interest, they said.
South Africa recorded a trade surplus of 2.040 billion rand in December from a 378 million rand surplus in November, bringing the year surplus to 10.577 billion rand against 4.884 billion in 1995.
Although gold shares and mining houses suffered the brunt of the weaker bullion price, fourth quarter gold mining results from Anglo were generally well received, dealers said.
Anglo said on Thursday its gold mines posted available profit up nine percent to 340.8 million rand in the quarter to end December, 1996.
But although some mining stocks retraced from earlier losses, this was shortlived.
"It does not matter what the companies report, people are wary on the bullion price. They see it reaching $345," a dealer said.

At the end of trade, the gold index had dropped 24.8 points or 1.8 percent to a fresh one year low of 1,353.2. The industrial index lost 63.5 points to 8,083.1 and together they dragged down the overall index 38.9 points to 6,717.9.
Dealers said the market would look to Wall Street for direction on Friday.
De Beers gained 225 cents to 139.25 rand, SA Breweries dropped 150 cents to 123.25 rand and Engen slid 10 cents to 28.50 rand.
Freegold was 105 cents weaker at 31.45 rand, Kloof lost a rand to 32.75 rand and Vaal Reefs shed 700 cents to 298 rand.
Richemont lost 200 cents, or 3.05 percent, to 63.50 rand. Dealers said it appeared as if "something was going on" in the share after it was pushed firmer in Europe overnight.

Some dealers, however, poured water on the speculation, saying it was normal daily trade as the share normally trades in heavy volumes. It was the third most active share on the exchange on volume worth over 44 million rand.

South African industrial equity futures were weaker in late trade with the March all-share contract at 6,232/45 from 6,278 and the industrial contract at 7,935/44 from 7,978. Bullion weighed on gold contracts with the March future at 920/40 from 975.
